transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I came in because... I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. It's hard to say out loud, but sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew.
Over the past few weeks, have you experienced any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or had racing thoughts and many ideas coming at once?

No, I haven't felt like that at all. Honestly, it's been the exact opposite. I barely have the energy to get out of bed, let alone feel energetic or have racing thoughts. I've just been... tired. All the time.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, where you felt this depressed and hopeless for an extended period of time?

No, not really. I mean... I've felt down before, just normal bad days, but never anything like this. I've never had a time where I felt this completely hopeless for weeks on end. This is all new to me.
How long have you been feeling this way — this persistent tiredness, hopelessness, and difficulty getting out of bed?
It's been... about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband got hurt, and it just hasn't lifted since.

You mentioned this started a few months after your husband got hurt. Would you say that event is what triggered these feelings of hopelessness and the difficulty getting out of bed, or do you think you would have felt this way regardless of what happened to him?

I don't really know. I mean, it definitely started after his accident, so... I guess that must be what triggered it. But I don't know if I would have felt this way anyway. It's hard to say. I just know that's when things started getting really bad, and I haven't been able to shake it since.
Since your husband's accident, have you had unwanted memories or flashbacks of that event coming back to you, even when you don't want them to?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I think about the accident sometimes, obviously, because it changed everything, but... it's not like a flashback. I don't feel like I'm reliving it or having memories pop into my head when I don't want them to. It's just... the reality of what happened, you know? But no unwanted memories like that.

If your husband's condition were to improve significantly or if the situation with him were to resolve, do you think your feelings of hopelessness and the difficulty getting out of bed would also improve, or do you feel like these feelings have taken on a life of their own at this point?

I... honestly, I don't think it would change anything. I mean, I'd be glad if he got better, of course. But this heaviness... it just feels like it's a part of me now. It's like it has a life of its own, yeah. Even if everything was perfect, I just... I don't see how I'd suddenly be able to get out of bed and feel normal again. It's just too deep.
